text: Read carefully the local newspaper article printed in the Reading Booklet Insert about student
councils in schools. Then answer Section 1, Question 1 on this Question Paper.
Imagine you are a pupil in Mr Aziz’s school.
Write a letter to him, in which you:
• identify and discuss his views against student councils
• evaluate why and how a school council could be good for everybody.
Base your letter on what you have read in the article, but be careful to use your own words.
Write between 1½ to 2 sides, allowing for the size of your handwriting.
Up to 10 marks are available for the content of your answer, and up to 15 marks for the
Write about two sides, allowing for the size of your handwriting, on one of the following questions.
Up to 13 marks are available for the content and structure of your answer, and up to 12 marks
are available for the style and accuracy of your writing.

How important are ambitions in your life and the lives of other young adults?
OR

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘There’s no place for art or music in the school curriculum these days.’ How far do you agree?
Descriptive Writing

You are waiting outside a room where you are to undergo an important interview. Describe
your surroundings and your feelings as you wait.
OR

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the scene at a station or airport where arriving passengers are met by friends and
relatives.
Narrative Writing

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Write a story entitled ‘The Storm’.
OR

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘The truth had to come out in the end.’ Write a story which ends with these words.
